correctness.rationale: For every 0<alpha<1 the constant and first cosine moments of any uniformly convergent series are respectively a sin(pi alpha)/(pi alpha) and alpha²/(1-alpha²) times that. Nonnegativity against 1-cos t contradicts alpha>=1/sqrt2, including equality, after excluding identically-zero restrictions via the first sine moment and full integer Fourier orthogonality. For alpha<1/sqrt2 the Poisson kernel with r=alpha²/(1-alpha²) agrees exactly on [-pi,pi] with a*cos(alpha*t) plus the absolutely summable coefficients c_n=2r^n+2(-1)^n alpha²/(n²-alpha²), n>=2. Translation preserves the frequency family. The proof handles all real coefficient phases and every interval; 344 checker assertions are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: Exact claim comparison: Haraux 2026 proves a sufficient ell2 frequency-perturbation criterion, which in the one-defect family applies only for alpha>1-1/(sqrt(8)*pi), whereas the new theorem proves the sharp alpha>=1/sqrt(2) boundary and explicit positive waveforms below it. The 1985 periodic-subspace statements inspected on pp. 58, 59, 61, 65, 69 do not state this exact threshold. Searches of published mathematical records for replacement, moment ratio and Poisson construction returned no equivalent or stronger coverage. Bibliographic risk of unexamined older equivalences remains, but no decisive source contradicts originality.
residual_risks: The complete 1985 and 2015 texts were not exhaustively inspected: an equivalent sharp special case could exist in unexamined material.
Search coverage is not an exhaustive proof of bibliographic novelty.

value.rationale: A natural one-defect stress test of Haraux 2026 receives a complete sharp two-sided classification at alpha=1/sqrt2 rather than a slightly improved sufficient ell2 constant. Explicit Poisson reconstruction gives strictly positive almost-periodic mean-zero signals throughout a full forbidden window below the boundary, including 1/2<alpha<1/sqrt2 where a lone cosine cannot stay positive. The dual moment mechanism is structural and testable in extensions, without claiming to solve the unrestricted frequency-gap problem.
